name: Field
layerWhy: It asks one question; answering a whole form is a cell's job.
promise: One question, with its label, a description when needed, and what's wrong with the answer right under it.
expectation: A visible label above a control the browser owns, and a message that appears only when there is something to say.
evidence: After the person has had their go, a wrong answer shows the danger edge and a message under the control that says what to type, in the person's words; optional fields are marked "Optional".
behaviour: The control stays native: autofill, the phone's keyboard and pasting work.
Validates on leaving the field, on input once shown, and on submit.
Messages come from the browser's validity, worded by PRIMAL_MESSAGES; [primalControl]="error" wins.
A search box, a choice, a slider or a colour is never marked Optional.
context: Wherever the product asks the person something. Not for showing a value that can't change; that is a detail.
relationships: The label is the question; the description says what to give; the message says what to fix.
Inside a group, a radio's message belongs to the group.
accessibility: The label is a <label for>; description and message are linked with aria-describedby.
aria-invalid when wrong; "Error:" read before the message.
The message region is polite, so it is announced as it speaks.
failures: Never an error before the person has had their go.
Never a placeholder as the label.
do: Mark what is optional, not what is required.
Size the control to the answer.
dont: A field without a visible label.
Errors in a banner far from the field.

usage.markup:
<primal-field label="Email" description="We only use it to send receipts.">
  <input primalControl type="email" autocomplete="email" required />
</primal-field>
